page: Microsoft Azure M64ms is an x86_64 memory-optimized virtual machine running on the Microsoft Hyper-V hypervisor. It features 64 dedicated vCPUs mapped to 32 physical Intel Xeon 8280L cores with hyper-threading enabled. The processor operates at a base frequency of 2.7 GHz and includes a 105 MB L3 cache. The server is equipped with 1792.0 GB of RAM, providing 28.0 GB of memory per physical core, alongside 2097 GB of local SSD storage.

Benchmark data indicates a clear performance profile. Single-core performance is weak, with stress-ng, Geekbench, and single-threaded compression tests scoring in the bottom 10%. However, multi-core performance scales to average levels, as shown by stress-ng and Geekbench multi-core scores. Memory subsystem performance is a key highlight, with uncached read-only large block memory bandwidth reaching a strong 196.25 GB/sec, placing it in the top 25%. Other memory operations, database transactions, and Redis SET operations perform in the average tier.

Given its massive memory-to-vCPU ratio and local SSD capacity, the M64ms offers high resource density for memory-bound workloads. The trade-off involves lower single-core CPU performance in exchange for massive RAM capacity. This configuration is highly suited for large-scale in-memory databases, enterprise relational databases, heavy data caching layers, and memory-intensive enterprise applications that do not require high single-threaded compute speeds.
